headline: Armed assailants storm home in Mohammadpur; attack video goes viral
summary: A shocking video circulating online shows a group of individuals armed with sharp weapons entering a residence in Mohammadpur and launching an assault. Authorities are investigating the incident.
details: A brazen attack has been captured on camera in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, where a group of armed assailants forcibly entered a home. The incident, which occurred recently, has sent shockwaves through the community after a video of the assault went viral on social media.

The video footage shows the attackers wielding sharp weapons as they confront individuals inside the residence. The motive behind the attack and the identities of the assailants are currently unknown, prompting an urgent investigation by local law enforcement.

The rapid spread of the video online has raised concerns about public safety and the ease with which such violent acts are being recorded and shared. Authorities are urging citizens to provide any information that could help identify and apprehend the perpetrators.
caption:

headline_marked: Over 100,000 [[affected by worsening floods]] in Bandarban
headline: Over 100,000 affected by worsening floods in Bandarban
summary: Heavy rainfall and rising river levels have inundated thousands of homes across 29 unions, disrupting communication and power in the district.
details: Six consecutive days of heavy rainfall, flash floods from upstream, and rising water levels in the Sangu and Matamuhuri rivers have left more than 100,000 people in distress in Bandarban.
Floodwaters have inundated thousands of homes in over 500 villages across 29 of the district's 34 unions, affecting the majority of the region.
Over 5,000 residents from landslide-prone areas have been evacuated, with 4,600 people taking shelter in 54 evacuation centres.
Fresh flooding was reported in Bandarban town and upazilas including Thanchi, Ruma, Rowangchhari, Lama, and Alikadam after overnight rainfall.
Road communication between the district headquarters and upazilas, as well as the rest of the country, has been severely disrupted, leaving boats as the only means of transport in many areas.
Power outages and mobile network disruptions have further compounded the suffering of residents during the crisis.
The Sangu river is flowing above the danger level at 16.81 metres, while the Matamuhuri river stands at 12.13 metres, according to the Water Development Board.
The army, Fire Service, police, and volunteers are conducting rescue and relief operations as authorities remain on alert for further flooding and landslides.
The district meteorological office recorded 88mm of rainfall in the last 24 hours and warns that rain is likely to continue until tomorrow.
caption:
Over 100,000 people are in distress as severe flooding hits Bandarban, with thousands of homes inundated across 29 unions.

Six consecutive days of heavy rainfall, flash floods from upstream, and rising water levels in the Sangu and Matamuhuri rivers have left more than 100,000 people in distress in Bandarban.

Floodwaters have inundated thousands of homes in over 500 villages across 29 of the district's 34 unions, affecting the majority of the region.

Over 5,000 residents from landslide-prone areas have been evacuated, with 4,600 people taking shelter in 54 evacuation centres.

Fresh flooding was reported in Bandarban town and upazilas including Thanchi, Ruma, Rowangchhari, Lama, and Alikadam after overnight rainfall.

Road communication between the district headquarters and upazilas, as well as the rest of the country, has been severely disrupted, leaving boats as the only means of transport in many areas.

Power outages and mobile network disruptions have further compounded the suffering of residents during the crisis.

The Sangu river is flowing above the danger level at 16.81 metres, while the Matamuhuri river stands at 12.13 metres, according to the Water Development Board.

The army, Fire Service, police, and volunteers are conducting rescue and relief operations as authorities remain on alert for further flooding and landslides.

The district meteorological office recorded 88mm of rainfall in the last 24 hours and warns that rain is likely to continue until tomorrow.
